newsitem.title: USA: US PLAINS FED CATTLE MARKET AT STANDSTILL-FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: US PLAINS FED CATTLE MARKET AT STANDSTILL-FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade near midday Monday remained at a standstill, with no reported sales, feedlot sources said.
Bids were scattered at $63.00 to $64.00 per cwt, steady to $1.00 lower from last sales late last week at $64.00. Owners passed the bids and were pricing cattle at $65.00 to $66.00, sources said.

Steep declines in beef prices last week were seen weighing on fed cattle prices this week although active sales at the lower prices spurred speculation that beef prices were near a bottom and could be poised to trend higher.

Beef prices at midday Monday were quoted $0.16 to $0.30 per cwt higher, with 47 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $103.47, up $0.21 from Friday, USDA statistics showed.

Beef demand last week was stimulated by a steep price drop and also was attributed to early retailer booking of beef orders for Labor Day weekend holiday late this month, sources noted. The U.S. Labor Day holiday is on September 1.
Fed cattle prices this week also were seen pressured by a large carryover of cattle from last week's showlists.
